slots_and_copies.name: header
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Treated as the single master record (magic + Group A checksum); blank EAMA magic triggers first-boot populate path in FUN_08026c30.

slots_and_copies.name: group_a_primary
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Live sum-of-bytes checksum compared against stored checksum at 0x02-0x03; if mismatched and group_a_backup matches, group_a_backup is copied over this slot.

slots_and_copies.name: group_a_backup
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Mirror of group_a_primary; whichever copy's live checksum matches the cached/stored checksum is authoritative and overwrites the other.

slots_and_copies.name: group_b_primary
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Same mirrored-pair checksum selection pattern as Group A (structurally identical code path), unverified field offsets because this sample is blank.

slots_and_copies.name: group_c_primary
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Same mirrored-pair checksum selection pattern as Group A, unverified offsets (blank sample).

slots_and_copies.name: group_d_primary
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Same mirrored-pair checksum selection pattern as Group A, unverified offsets (blank sample).

slots_and_copies.name: unaddressed_erased_region
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Never addressed by any traced sector index (sectors 36-63); remains raw erased EEPROM (0xFF).

checksums.name: group_a_checksum
checksums.formula_detail: 16-bit little-endian accumulator = (sum of all 16 bytes in covered range) mod 0x10000, no carry propagation beyond 16 bits, no seed.

checksums.name: group_b_checksum
checksums.formula_detail: Same sum-of-bytes-mod-0x10000 algorithm as group_a_checksum, applied over the 40-byte Group B range; exact stored offset unconfirmed (sample is all-zero, so a zero computed sum trivially matches a zero stored field at any candidate offset).

checksums.name: group_c_checksum
checksums.formula_detail: Same algorithm as group_a_checksum over the 40-byte Group C range; stored offset unconfirmed for the same reason as group_b_checksum.

checksums.name: group_d_checksum
checksums.formula_detail: Same algorithm as group_a_checksum over the 40-byte Group D range; stored offset unconfirmed for the same reason as group_b_checksum.

checksums.name: group_loader_checksum
checksums.formula_detail: Sum-of-bytes mod 0x10000 over a 40-byte group, same algorithm family, used by the per-slot runtime loader (distinct call site from the boot-time validator).

io_driver_functions.notes: Shared DMA3 transfer primitive: programs DMA3 src/dest/count-control registers, sets start bit 0x80000000, busy-waits on control-register bit 0x8000. Used by both the read and write paths; role listed as 'read' only because the schema enum has no 'transfer' option, but it is direction-agnostic.
EEPROM read of one 8-byte sector: bit-packs 6-bit sector address, issues DMA3 request tagged 0x30000, unpacks 64-bit response into 4x u16 words. Bounds-checked against a device-size table.

EEPROM write of one 8-byte sector: bit-packs data+address, issues DMA3 request tagged 0x430000, busy-waits on EEPROM data-line bit 0, bracketed by interrupt-mask toggle functions 0x080b6998/0x080b69fc.
Verify = read-back (via 0x080b6ac0) + compare 4 words against expected buffer; returns 0x8000 on mismatch. Used as the post-write verification step.
Sets an interrupt-enable-style bit (8<<N) in an MMIO-shadowed register immediately before the write busy-wait in 0x080b6b78. Exact IRQ line not confirmed from this trace slice (HYPOTHESIS).
Clears the same bit set by 0x080b6998, restoring prior interrupt-mask state after the write busy-wait completes.
Device/bank size-table probe used only by the presence/size-detect gate, not per-sector I/O.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Boot-time save validator entry: first calls the EEPROM presence/size-detect guard before touching any sector.
caller_chains.how_mapped: Traced by reading the first statement of FUN_08026c30 in decompiled.c, which calls FUN_0802687c; FUN_0802687c in turn loops on func_0x080b6960 up to 3 times. Not present in callgraph.json's extraction window.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Boot-time validator reads Group A primary copy (sector 2, count 2) and backup copy (sector 0x13, count 2) to compute live checksums.
ram_fields_updated: 0x10-0x1F (RAM mirror of Group A primary, exact IWRAM/EWRAM address unresolved)
caller_chains.how_mapped: Grepped decompiled.c for every call site of func_0x08026934 inside FUN_08026c30 and cross-referenced the sector-index literals (0, 0x13, 4, 0x15, 9, 0x1a, 0xe, 0x1f) against the 8-bytes-per-sector addressing scheme to recover file byte offsets.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Boot-time validator repairs whichever copy of a mirrored group failed its checksum comparison by writing the good copy's bytes over the stale copy, then verifies by read-back.
ram_fields_updated: in-RAM scratch buffer used as the write source, copied from the sibling good copy's just-read buffer
caller_chains.how_mapped: Grepped decompiled.c for every call site of func_0x08026a30 inside FUN_08026c30; confirmed FUN_08026a30 itself performs write-then-verify by reading its own body (first loop calls 0x080b6b78, second loop calls 0x080b6c5c).

caller_chains.trigger_context: Runtime per-slot loader (distinct from boot-time validator) reads one 40-byte group selected by a parameter-indexed sector lookup table, validates its own sum-of-bytes checksum, and falls back to the backup-copy sector index on mismatch.
caller_chains.how_mapped: Grepped decompiled.c for func_0x08026934 call sites outside FUN_08026c30; found this second, independent caller at FUN_08028190, confirming the sector-read wrapper is shared by two distinct higher-level consumers.

fields.name: header_reserved_0
fields.update_mechanism: Written as part of header sector-pair (sector 0) write-verify in FUN_08026a30(0,...,2); not individually addressed by any branch in the traced code.
fields.evidence: Always zero in the only available sample; no code reads or branches on this sub-range specifically.

fields.name: group_a_checksum_field
fields.update_mechanism: Computed as sum-of-bytes mod 0x10000 over 0x10-0x1F in FUN_08026c30, written back via FUN_08026a30(0,...,2) whenever the header sector-pair needs repair.
fields.evidence: Python recomputation of sum(data[0x10:0x20]) & 0xFFFF against saves/cap-00-future-0.sav equals the stored u16-LE value at 0x02-0x03 exactly (0x00a8 == 0x00a8).

fields.name: magic_EAMA
fields.update_mechanism: Part of the header sector-pair; written once at first-boot populate time, read at every boot as the blank-vs-populated gate.
fields.evidence: Literal byte match against decompiled.c's header-sector handling and the real .sav bytes.

fields.name: header_reserved_1
fields.update_mechanism: Remainder of sector 1 (second half of the header sector-pair); no code branches on this sub-range specifically.

fields.name: group_a_reserved_0
fields.update_mechanism: Part of the checksummed Group A block; covered by group_a_checksum_field but not individually branched on.
fields.evidence: Always zero in sample; only mapped as 'covered by the proven checksum range', not independently.

fields.name: group_a_value_1
fields.update_mechanism: Part of the checksummed Group A block; no code path in the traced slice reads or branches on this specific sub-field, so neither its endianness nor its semantic purpose is confirmed.
fields.evidence: Nonzero bytes 0x4e 0x20 observed at this offset; value is covered by the proven group_a_checksum_field, so its presence is confirmed but its meaning is not.

fields.name: group_a_reserved_1
fields.update_mechanism: Part of the checksummed Group A block.

fields.name: group_a_value_2
fields.update_mechanism: Part of the checksummed Group A block; same caveat as group_a_value_1.
fields.evidence: Nonzero bytes 0x27 0x10 observed at this offset; covered by the proven checksum but meaning not confirmed.

fields.name: group_a_reserved_2
fields.update_mechanism: Part of the checksummed Group A block.

fields.name: group_a_trailing_byte
fields.update_mechanism: Last byte of the checksummed Group A block (offset 0x1F); no code path branches on it directly in the traced slice.
fields.evidence: Nonzero value 3 observed; could be a small counter or flag, covered by the proven checksum but unconfirmed semantically.

fields.name: group_b_primary_block
fields.update_mechanism: Same architecture as Group A (read via FUN_08026934(4,...,5), write-verify via FUN_08026a30(4,...,5)), but entirely unpopulated in this sample.
fields.evidence: Blank/all-zero in the only available sample; structure inferred from code only.

fields.name: group_c_primary_block
fields.update_mechanism: Same architecture as Group A (sector 9, count 5), unpopulated in this sample.
fields.evidence: Blank/all-zero; structure inferred from code only.

fields.name: group_d_primary_block
fields.update_mechanism: Same architecture as Group A (sector 0xe, count 5), unpopulated in this sample.
fields.evidence: Blank/all-zero; structure inferred from code only.

fields.name: group_a_backup_block
fields.update_mechanism: Mirror of group_a_primary via sector 0x13, count 2; selected/repaired by the same checksum-comparison logic in FUN_08026c30.
fields.evidence: Python byte-comparison data[0x10:0x20] == data[0x98:0xa8] is True against the real .sav file.

fields.name: group_b_backup_block
fields.update_mechanism: Mirror of group_b_primary via sector 0x15, count 5.
fields.evidence: Blank/all-zero; mirror relationship inferred from code only (both copies blank, so equality is consistent but unverified as a meaningful mirror).

fields.name: group_c_backup_block
fields.update_mechanism: Mirror of group_c_primary via sector 0x1a, count 5.

fields.name: group_d_backup_block
fields.update_mechanism: Mirror of group_d_primary via sector 0x1f, count 5.

fields.name: unaddressed_erased_region
fields.update_mechanism: Never addressed by any traced sector index (max observed sector+count reaches sector 35 / byte 0x11F); remains raw erased-EEPROM default.
fields.evidence: All bytes 0xFF in the real .sav, consistent with no write/read path in decompiled.c ever targeting sectors 36-63.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip a bit in group_a_value_1 (0x12-0x13) without updating the checksum at 0x02-0x03.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: On next boot, FUN_08026c30 detects the primary-copy checksum mismatch, finds the backup copy (0x9A-0x9B) still checksum-consistent, and auto-repairs the primary copy from the backup.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Corrupt both group_a_value_1 (0x12) and the mirrored byte at group_a_backup (0x9A) so neither copy's live checksum matches 0x02-0x03 and the two copies disagree with each other.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Both-copies-bad case: error bitmask gets a Group A failure bit set and func_0x080287f8 (fatal/alert handler) is invoked instead of silent auto-repair.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Change group_a_value_1 (0x12-0x13) to a new value and recompute+write the correct sum-of-bytes checksum into 0x02-0x03, keeping the backup copy identical.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Save is accepted as fully valid (no repair/fatal path); any in-game observable difference tied to this value would be the first evidence toward its semantic meaning.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Zero out the EAMA magic bytes.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Save is treated as blank/uninitialized; FUN_08026c30's first-boot populate-and-write path re-runs, effectively resetting the header and Group A on next write.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Write non-0xFF garbage into the unaddressed erased region (0x120-0x1FF).
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: No observable effect at all (negative control confirming this region is genuinely unaddressed dead space, not an undiscovered fifth group).

open_questions: Semantic meaning of group_a_value_1 (0x12-0x13, raw bytes 4e 20) and group_a_value_2 (0x16-0x17, raw bytes 27 10) is unknown; no traced code reads or branches on these sub-fields independently of the group-level checksum.
Endianness of group_a_value_1 / group_a_value_2 is unconfirmed; only the checksum (which is endianness-agnostic, a byte sum) was verified.

Exact stored-checksum byte offsets for Group B, Group C, and Group D could not be confirmed because all three groups are entirely zero-filled in the only available .sav sample; a populated-save sample is required.
Semantic meaning of group_a_trailing_byte (0x1F, value 3) is unknown.
The IRQ line toggled by 0x080b6998/0x080b69fc around the EEPROM write busy-wait in 0x080b6b78 is not identified.

callgraph.json under-reports true callers for the MMIO seed functions (0x080b6ac0, 0x080b6b78) because its extraction window is limited to a 2-hop neighborhood; the real caller chain up through 0x08026934/0x08026a30/0x08026c30/0x08028190 had to be manually recovered from decompiled.c and should be treated as more authoritative than callgraph.json alone for this release.

No gameplay-triggered (non-boot-time) write path into the save-writer layer (FUN_08026a30) was found within the available trace depth; only the boot-time validator/repair path and the per-slot runtime loader (read-only observed) were confirmed to reach the hardware layer.
